title: Conductors he worked under and Phil Moore's Astaire film
summary: Before Nat, Lee worked under the Bakaleinikoffs, Stoloff, Heindorf and others, and played drums for Phil Moore's score for Fred Astaire's One for My Baby.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: And when I started conducting for Nat, it was really a simple thing, and the guys thought that I had been conducting for ages, but I had not. And then again, I had worked under so many good conductors, you know -- I worked under both Bachalegnakoffs, you know, I worked under Morris Stoloff, I worked under a guy at Warner Brothers, Ray Heinrichk, George Estolle, Johnny Greene, by the time I was with Nat, I had worked under all these people -- Johnny Greene and George Estolle, and Phil Moore was not bad, either.
He did some conducting at RKO Studios when he would make the arrangements. Were you aware of that?
No, I did not know that.

You know, Phil Moore did the movie at RKO for Fred Astaire -- that's where the song, 'One More for The Road' came from? 11 One for my baby, and one for the road, 11 when he was dancing on the bar and kicking over the glasses?
Well, Phil Moore did all the music for that, and I played all the drums for that.
Yeah. So that was with Constantine Bachaleynokoff; that was the other one. The other was Misha; the one that I spoke to you about.
